verdict.headline: This NDA is highly one-sided, imposing perpetual secrecy without exceptions while leaving your own shared tender data completely unprotected.
summary: The agreement defines your confidentiality obligations to last in perpetuity with zero standard exceptions, even for public info or legal orders.
The Discloser takes no confidentiality duties toward your tender or pricing and reserves the right to terminate at will while you stay bound.
You are subject to an uncapped indemnity covering legal costs on a full indemnity basis for any breach by you or your staff.

Ordinary commercial NDAs always carve out public domain information, prior knowledge, independent development, and disclosures required by legal authorities.
findings.standard: Standard NDAs carve out information that is public, already known, received from a third party without breach, or required to be disclosed by law or court order.
findings.suggested_ask: Please add the standard exceptions for information that is public, already known, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law or court order.

A 12-month post-termination non-compete restricts you from providing design or web development services to other digital agencies in Malaysia.

verdict.headline: This tenancy imposes high risks including a discretionary deposit forfeiture, unilateral rent increases, and full structural repair costs.
summary: The agreement allows the landlord to retain your RM20,400 deposit at its sole discretion without explanation under clause 4.2.
The landlord can unilaterally hike the rent by any amount on 14 days' notice under clause 5.1, while disallowing exit or objection under clause 5.2.
You are made liable for all building and structural repairs under clause 6.1, and subject to extra-judicial lockouts under clause 8.1.

findings.why_risky: The landlord can arbitrarily forfeit your security deposit without providing any justification or accounting for actual losses. A security deposit should only cover unpaid rent, utilities, or documented damage beyond fair wear and tear.
findings.standard: Security deposits for commercial tenancies are typically 2 to 3 months' rent, refundable within 14 to 30 days after handover, with deductions strictly limited to proven arrears or damage beyond fair wear and tear.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the security deposit refundable within 21 days of handover back, with deductions limited to unpaid rent and utilities and damage beyond fair wear and tear, each shown by a written list or receipts.

findings.title: Remaining term rent due on early exit
findings.quote: If the Tenant ends this Agreement early in any other way, the Tenant shall pay the Landlord all Rent for the remainder of the Term, as agreed compensation.
findings.why_risky: Demanding all rent for the unexpired term as compensation ignores the landlord's obligation to mitigate damages by re-letting. Malaysian courts under s 75 of the Contracts Act 1950 assess reasonable compensation rather than automatic enforcement of full unexpired rent sums.
findings.standard: Early termination fees should reflect a capped, proportionate amount (such as 1 to 2 months' rent) or actual losses incurred while the landlord diligently attempts to re-let the premises.
findings.suggested_ask: Please let the tenant leave on 2 months' written notice after month 6, in return for a fee of one month's rent and the return of the balance of the deposit, with the landlord to try to re-let.
